blocks.text: `_concept/` is one root folder in the project. It holds 14 first-level entries: three root files ([[e-brief-md]], [[e-goals-md]], [[e-glossary-md]]) and eleven numbered folders from [[e-01-meta]] to [[e-11-build]]. 25 of 31 skills write into it. Each skill names its paths in `metadata.artifacts.produces`. 4 entries have more than one writer.

The numbers sort the folders for the reader. They do not give the write order: [[e-10-blueprint-datamodel]] is written before [[e-05-features]], and [[e-09-mockup]] comes after the screens. Everything before [[e-11-build]] is design. Everything in [[e-11-build]] is build.

sections.title: What each folder holds and who writes it
sections.question: q1

blocks.text: The tree has 61 entries: 25 folders, 32 files and 4 patterns. A pattern is one file per feature, screen or featureset. Each row shows the description from the contract, the writer skill, the number of reader skills and the first write step. [[e-02-grounding]] holds everything from outside the project: [[e-02-grounding-onboarding]], [[e-02-grounding-research]] and the graded findings of `concept-reverse`: [[e-02-grounding-findings-index-md]], [[e-02-grounding-findings-routes-md]], [[e-02-grounding-findings-screens-md]], [[e-02-grounding-findings-datamodel-md]], [[e-02-grounding-findings-stack-md]], [[e-02-grounding-findings-brand-md]], [[e-02-grounding-findings-brief-seeds-md]]. The badges filter the tree and the map in the section on readers.

blocks.hint: Click a badge to hide or show entries. The map of readers below follows the same filter.

sections.title: What each project type never grows
sections.question: q2

blocks.text: `concept-scope` reads `project_type` and resolves it against one of 6 profiles. A profile lists the artifacts a project of that type never grows. 4 types never grow journeys, screens, brand, behaviors or mockups: `api-service`, `cli-tool`, `data-pipeline`, `library`. A `library` also never grows a data model. A `web-app` grows the full tree.

A flow grows an entry when a writer of that entry is a node of the flow. [[f-appbuilder-standard]] grows all first-level entries. [[f-appbuilder-mvp]] has 11 nodes and skips 5 of them: [[e-03-brand]], [[e-06-behaviors]], [[e-07-screens]], [[e-08-dossiers]], [[e-09-mockup]]. The last column gives the step of [[f-appbuilder-standard]] that writes the entry first.

sections.title: The order in which folders are written
sections.question: q4

blocks.text: The diagram follows [[f-appbuilder-standard]] from `scope` to the end. Each box is a step that writes an entry for the first time. The order is domain language, then data model, then features and screens, then architecture, then mockups, then build. The data model (`10_blueprint/datamodel/`) comes before every feature, so no feature skill coins an entity name.

blocks.text: The map joins the 14 first-level entries with the skills that read or write them. A green edge is a write from `metadata.artifacts.produces`. A blue edge is a `hard` prerequisite: the skill stops without the file. A dashed edge is a `soft` prerequisite or a `requires` id. [[e-brief-md]] has the most readers: 14 skills.

sections.title: How one feature spreads across the tree
sections.question: q8

blocks.text: A feature owns files in 6 places. It shares 4 more files with other features. The feature spec is the center. Its `<feature_slug>` names the screen folder and the dossier. Frontmatter fields join the rest: `story_refs`, `data_entities[]`, `screens:` and `implements:`. On the build side, the ledger names the spec in `feature_ref`, and [[e-11-build-trace-yaml]] joins the feature to its slices and commits.

sections.title: Where the tree and the skills disagree
sections.question: q9

blocks.text: The gate accepts a written path when it lies under a folder of the tree. So 9 written paths are valid but the tree does not name them. Most are files inside a folder the tree describes in words. The other direction also has gaps: entries that the tree lists and that no skill names on its own.

No skill declares a write of [[e-11-build-decisions-md]]. The tree lists it at `contracts/concept_structure.md:89`.
No skill writes into [[e-02-grounding-seeds]]. That is by design: the contract says "material the user dropped in; nothing generates it".

2 entries under [[e-02-grounding-standards]] have no writer of their own: [[e-02-grounding-standards-index-yml]], [[e-02-grounding-standards-domain]]. [[s-quality-standards]] declares only the folder.

7 entries under [[e-02-grounding-findings]] have no writer of their own: [[e-02-grounding-findings-index-md]], [[e-02-grounding-findings-routes-md]], [[e-02-grounding-findings-screens-md]], [[e-02-grounding-findings-datamodel-md]], [[e-02-grounding-findings-stack-md]], [[e-02-grounding-findings-brand-md]], [[e-02-grounding-findings-brief-seeds-md]]. [[s-concept-research]], [[s-concept-reverse]], [[s-design-brand]] declare only the folder.

blocks.text: The contract states one numbering rule and five naming rules. The gate checks the singular and plural rule.

items: The first level has a number. Nothing below it has a number. (`contracts/concept_structure.md:104`)
The number is the only order signal. The host sidebar removes the prefix before it shows the name. (`contracts/concept_structure.md:106`)
The numbers are contiguous. A twelfth folder renumbers every folder after it. (`contracts/concept_structure.md:112`)
File names are lowercase and hyphenated. One artifact has exactly one path. (`contracts/concept_structure.md:117`)
Two siblings never differ only by singular and plural. (`contracts/concept_structure.md:119`)
`shell` is a reserved slug under [[e-07-screens]]. (`contracts/concept_structure.md:123`)
Folders under [[e-05-features]] and [[e-07-screens]] are slugs: lowercase, hyphenated, no number. (`contracts/concept_structure.md:124`)
Each folder under [[e-02-grounding-research-step-skill-name]] has the name of the skill that sent the research. (`contracts/concept_structure.md:126`)
